newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Pharma Vision buys Novartis shares - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pharma Vision buys Novartis shares - paper.

text.p: Pharma Vision, part of Swiss financier Martin Ebner's BZ Group Holding, is buying shares of life sciences group Novartis, Swiss weekly business paper HandelsZeitung said on Thursday.
Quoting unnamed sources, HandelsZeitung said Ebner had been actively buying Novartis shares for the last few weeks to take advantage of the potential for future rises.
Kurt Schiltknecht, member of BZ board and chief executive of Pharma Vision, declined to comment on the article.
On Friday morning BZ Bank will announce the participations by the BZ Group's investment trusts.
Pharma Vision is one of the world's largest investment trust specialising in the healthcare area. At the end of 1996, its portfolio was valued at 5.2 billion Swiss francs.

Ebner said in January that BZ Group's investment trusts were in the process of diversifying and one example was Pharma Vision's sale of some of its stake in Roche Holding AG to finance a stake in German Hoechst.
In May BZ Group also said that trusts BK Vision and Stillhalter Vision had built up their holdings in Winterthur Insurance to a combined 14.5 percent.
A further 5.5 percent stake is held directly by clients of BZ Bank.
The reason for the purchases of Winterthur was that the shares of Winterthur has underperformed other Swiss insurers, such as Zurich Group and Swiss Reinsurance.
